scenes.tts: Is dopamine the brain's pleasure signal? It is a common shortcut. Let's test it.
scenes.visual: A brain with a dopamine label and a smiley face, then a question mark. Title card: Wanting is not liking.
scenes.narration: Is dopamine the brain's pleasure signal? It is a common shortcut. Let's test it.

scenes.tts: Two things need separating. Wanting is the pull of a reward and its cues. Liking is the pleasure of the reward itself.
scenes.visual: Two labels: wanting, the pull; liking, the impact.
scenes.narration: Two things need separating. Wanting is the pull of a reward and its cues. Liking is the pleasure of the reward itself.

scenes.tts: How can you measure liking in a rat, without asking? Watch its face.
scenes.visual: An illustrated rat face, close up.
scenes.narration: How can you measure liking in a rat, without asking? Watch its face.

scenes.tts: Sweet tastes bring tongue protrusions. Bitter tastes bring gapes. These reactions can be scored from video.
scenes.visual: Drawn rat faces: tongue protrusions to sugar, a gape to bitter. Label: taste reactivity.
scenes.narration: Sweet tastes bring tongue protrusions. Bitter tastes bring gapes. These reactions can be scored from video.

scenes.tts: Rats whose forebrain dopamine was depleted with a neurotoxin stopped seeking food.
scenes.visual: A rat ignores a food dish. A 2 by 2 grid appears: rows dopamine down, dopamine up; columns seeks food, face to sugar.
scenes.narration: Rats whose forebrain dopamine was depleted with a neurotoxin stopped seeking food.

scenes.tts: If dopamine carried pleasure, what should their faces do when sugar is placed in the mouth?
scenes.visual: Sugar drop approaches the rat's mouth. Question mark in the face-to-sugar cell.
scenes.narration: If dopamine carried pleasure, what should their faces do when sugar is placed in the mouth?

scenes.visual: The question stays on screen; a small countdown ring runs.

scenes.tts: Their faces showed normal liking reactions. The seeking was gone, but the liking reactions remained.
scenes.visual: The grid fills in: dopamine down, seeking falls, face normal.
scenes.narration: Their faces showed normal liking reactions. The seeking was gone, but the liking reactions remained.

scenes.tts: Now the other direction. Mutant mice make little of the dopamine transporter, so extra dopamine stays outside the cells.
scenes.visual: A schematic striatal synapse with few transporters; extracellular dopamine dots crowd the gap. On screen: DAT about 10% of normal; about 70% more extracellular striatal dopamine.
scenes.narration: Now the other direction. Mutant mice make little of the dopamine transporter, so extra dopamine stays outside the cells.

scenes.tts: They reached sweet food sooner in a runway. They ran no faster. They just paused less on the way.
scenes.visual: A mouse runs a runway to sweet food with fewer pauses.
scenes.narration: They reached sweet food sooner in a runway. They ran no faster. They just paused less on the way.

scenes.tts: But their liking reactions to sugar were no stronger.
scenes.visual: The grid fills in: dopamine up, seeking rises, face not higher. Label: Peciña and colleagues, 2003.
scenes.narration: But their liking reactions to sugar were no stronger.

scenes.tts: So, in these tests, dopamine moved wanting, not liking.
scenes.visual: The seeking column glows; the face column stays flat.
scenes.narration: So, in these tests, dopamine moved wanting, not liking.

scenes.tts: Recall the burst that moves to cues. It is compatible with cues gaining pull, but whether it is wanting is debated.
scenes.visual: A light and a place in a cage glow as they take on pull. Label: compatible, debated.
scenes.narration: Recall the burst that moves to cues. It is compatible with cues gaining pull, but whether it is wanting is debated.

scenes.tts: Keep the scope. A lifelong mutation is not an acute drug, and an animal's face is not a human report.
scenes.visual: Scope card: lifelong mutation, not a drug; a face, not a human report.
scenes.narration: Keep the scope. A lifelong mutation is not an acute drug, and an animal's face is not a human report.

scenes.tts: Other researchers read the same results as changes in willingness to work, or in learning.
scenes.visual: Scope card adds: other readings, willingness to work, learning.
scenes.narration: Other researchers read the same results as changes in willingness to work, or in learning.

scenes.tts: Addictive drugs raise dopamine signalling, by different routes.
scenes.visual: A drug icon acting at the dopamine synapse, blocking or reversing the transporter.
scenes.narration: Addictive drugs raise dopamine signalling, by different routes.

scenes.tts: Incentive sensitization theory proposes that in susceptible people, repeated use can make cue-triggered wanting grow. It can grow out of proportion to liking.
scenes.visual: The cue's glow grows trial by trial while the liking face stays flat. Label: Robinson and Berridge.
scenes.narration: Incentive sensitization theory proposes that in susceptible people, repeated use can make cue-triggered wanting grow. It can grow out of proportion to liking.

scenes.tts: It offers one explanation for why craving can outlast enjoyment. It is a theory, and other accounts exist.
scenes.visual: Card: a theory; also habit, prefrontal control, withdrawal and stress.
scenes.narration: It offers one explanation for why craving can outlast enjoyment. It is a theory, and other accounts exist.

scenes.tts: In these tests, dopamine moved wanting, not liking. Its quick bursts mark better than predicted, and its pauses worse than predicted. They are not a direct measure of pleasure.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: dopamine moved wanting, not liking; bursts: better than predicted; pauses: worse.
scenes.narration: In these tests, dopamine moved wanting, not liking. Its quick bursts mark better than predicted, and its pauses worse than predicted. They are not a direct measure of pleasure.
